svg.title: Where a launching dispatch's claim is visible
svg.desc: Two timelines. At base, a dispatch mints its run id and publishes its claim only after the worktree, prompt and peer wiring, so a second dispatch arriving in that span reads no claim and launches a duplicate. At the change, the claim is published at the run id, so the second dispatch is refused naming the first run. A third panel shows the exclusion falsified: the dispatch refuses on the claim of the run id it just created.
svg.text: A dispatch holds its declared paths from its run id, not from its launch
Measured 2026-09-26: two dispatches launched a duplicate over the same paths, and a refusal named the claim of a run created moments earlier.
the span the paths are held invisibly: worktree, prompt, peer wiring
a second dispatch reads no claim, takes the same paths, launches a duplicate
at the change: the claim is published at the run id
the same span, now read by every peer
a second dispatch is refused, naming the first run
the exclusion falsified, both arms measured
the acceptance test with the exclusion in place: 4 passed, exit 0, one live pointer naming the run.
the same test with the exclusion dropped: the dispatch is refused by the claim of the run id it just created -
"write scope 'src/claimed.py' conflicts with live claim 'src/claimed.py' held by run 'r-...-node-claiming'" - the incident's shape.
Gate, both arms, one invocation: 84 passed at the change against 82 passed and 2 failed at base - the two failures are this node's added assertions.
